entry.title: Perspicacity
entry.content:
I learnt this new word: “perspicacity”.

You might be wondering why I am writing a blog post and not a flashcard for it. That is a fair thought! I’ll tell you why.

It is because I learnt this word from this small Tamil book.

This is exactly the thing I love about books. You never know where they’ll take you!

Before I tell you what the word means, I want to talk a little bit about the book.

The book is written in a language called Tamil. The title of the book translates to “Bright Future”.

The book is a transcript of a speech delivered by Vethathiri Maharishi. He created Manavalakalai Yoga (simplified yoga) that can be understood by anybody. The style of language used in the book is “Thooya Tamil” (pure Tamil). Here is the part that made me say wow: the book contains Tamil poems over 1,000 years old, explains the grammar of ancient Tamil poems and at the same time contains a little passage explaining the meaning of the word “perspicacity”!

Here is the quote from it:

Perspicacity என்றால் Quick insight of the mind linking past experiences, present circumstances and future results taking a right decision in right time and following and getting benefit.

With the advent of AI, I have been thinking about what I need to navigate this. I have come across some words people mention to describe what you need to succeed in AI: “moat”, “agency”, etc. - you needed most of them before AI too.

With AI, I think we need “perspicacity”. Here is my theory on why: AI is producing tons of code and documents a.k.a. AI slop. Now almost every engineer I talk to is feeling overwhelmed by it. I myself find it too much to digest and I would say that it is my number one blocker to doing hard things now.

So here is my advice to myself and to you (if you are looking to work better with AI): Do things that increase your perspicacity.

Do what again?

You need to be able to generate insights when you need them. Your mind has to be prepared for it. That means you have a certain level of clarity, learnings from past experiences, awareness about the present situation, and a sense of future results.

So do what you need to do to maximize the chance of the right insights arriving in your mind. That usually means:

  • Learn things and internalize what you think might help with new insights.
    • Example: While debugging a system, your knowledge of the words p50, p95, p99 is an insight that you can leverage to debug faster and more thoroughly. So it is your duty to learn and internalize p50, p95, p99 to the point that it occurs to you when you need it.
  • Prioritize your health.
    • Both physical and mental! Now this is the important part. In order for right insights to strike you at the right time you have to have a peaceful state of mind. Get good sleep, do things that make you happy, relax, meditate, journal, take naps: these might be some ways to achieve peace. Find and do what works for you!
  • Act on the insights.
    • This is agency!

Just ask “what is going to increase my perspicacity?” in a given situation and follow through.

Oh! and the closest thing to an answer to AI slop that I have found so far is to ask a lot of questions to it or make it ask a lot of questions to you (grill me skill). Vibe-coding isn’t going to give you insights. Trying to read through every line of code will make you feel left behind. You need to do something in the middle where you are able to generate insights! That usually means building a theory of your programs to serve you at the right time.

That’s all I have for now.

~ ~ ~ ~

Hope that gave you some insights!

entry.content:
Here is what I read from 6th to 18th October 2026.

Side note: I have been travelling for festive holidays here in India and doing a Harry Potter movie marathon (currently on part 7) during this period of time.

Blogs

  • How I manage my agents

    I want to look into as many people’s workflows as possible to learn whatever I can on how to best work with AI to build software.

  • You should all be asking way more questions

    Ask, ask, ask!

  • Ephemeral testing

  • Developers Should Read the Classics Too

    Excellent, loved it! I already have a stack of classics waiting for me, and Animal Farm is my top choice too.

  • You should never be angry at work

  • How to keep learning in the age of LLMs

    Learnt a new term: “self-efficacy”. I liked the way the blog post prompts you to think in how you can get better for the new AI age.

entry.title: Reading Log #7
entry.content:
Here is what I read from 18th September to 3rd October 2026.

Blogs

  • The revolt of the reader

    Discovered Pangram via this post. I haven’t run into blog posts where an LLM has written most of it — lucky that I don’t get to follow/stumble upon that part of the internet. But I have stumbled upon too many website copies being authored by LLMs and it makes me furious all the time.

  • ⭐ the senior engineer death spiral

    Must-read for any engineer.

  • Introducing System One Models & Jev

    A new day, a new thing in the AI world.

  • Jev means structured output is interesting again

    But as Nelson Elhage famously said, fast software doesn’t just mean we can do the same tasks faster, it means we can do entirely new kinds of tasks. What kinds of new programs can we write by injecting 100ms worth of dirt-cheap intelligence at various decision points?

  • Joy & Curiosity #100

    My usual read :)

  • ⭐ Grit your teeth and ship it

    Build momentum! — almost always the right way.

  • “Act now, apologize later”

    Fascinating — never thought this would be done like this in game dev.

  • Trying the Software factory pattern.

  • Three Sticky Notes

    I have been recently experimenting with using sticky notes for managing my TODOs. It has been working out okay some days and I go off track on some days. But I have to tell you this: it is so satisfying to crush the sticky note for a done task.

  • Joy & Curiosity #101

  • AI Has No Wisdom and Neither Will You

    Okay, finally somebody is making a prediction that I haven’t heard anyone tell.

  • Degrees of freedom

    Where there is a will, there is a way!

  • I don’t want the details

    A good CXO would make you feel that they trust you and steer you towards doing your best work at hard times. The trust part isn’t always obvious. For example, when a CXO says “I don’t want the details”, you might feel rudeness, but what it could mean might be different. Imposter syndrome could be at play. I believe it takes both the humans to operate with optimism in tough times to achieve great results!

  • Attention is all you have

    I have been opting more and more for the slow internet.

  • Burnout by the Kindness of Agents

    Mental overload is real!

Books

  • ⭐ ✅ How Will You Measure Your Life?

    (read 122 pages)

    I haven’t experienced something like this. The book belongs to a genre that I can’t explain. This is definitely one of the best books I have read this year. And it goes straight to my “suggest-to-anyone-as-a-must-read-book” list.

  • Digital Minimalism

    (read 64 pages)

    I already have a good hang of some parts of my digital life. But want to revise my way of using social media a bit.

  • Show Your Work!

    (read 36 pages)

  • Grandma’s Bag of Stories

    (read 5 pages)

    Bedtime stories!

  • Letters from a Stoic

    (read 3 pages)

    Where you arrive does not matter so much as what sort of person you are when you arrive there. — Letter XXVIII

  • The Daily Stoic

    (read 2 pages)

  • Tao Te Ching

    (read a few random pages)

    Those who are good I treat as good. Those who are not good I also treat as good. In so doing I gain in goodness. Those who are of good faith I have faith in. Those who are lacking in good faith I also have faith in. In so doing I gain in good faith.

entry.title: Reading Log #5
entry.content:
I have been travelling the past 2 weeks and mostly spent time with a book during my reading time.

Here is what I read from 24th August to 6th September 2026.

Blogs

  • The end of programming

    AI models have gotten so good that it is becoming trivial to produce a lot of code in a day. Almost unreasonable amount of code that it would take even days to read through and get into them. I have been facing similar situation recently. Dealing with them is going to get normal. Let us figure out how to navigate this!

  • Why I am shutting down my bookstore in New Delhi

    I have become interested in bookstores recently. Tried visiting some new ones. Trying to get a sense for how it would feel to run a bookstore. The one that was closed in the blog post was a 30 years old bookstore. If something that had been running for such a long time could come to close, why?

  • Small Models Have Arrived

  • What is a Harness?

    Good intro!

  • Rebuilding Linear’s delta sync read path

    Interesting. This has made a few more interesting questions to delve on. Going to explore a bit. What are inverted indexes? What is the purpose of GIN?

  • Revised Rules of Engineering Leadership

  • Huzzah

    Same sentiment as post that I shared at the top. Huge amounts of code are getting written with AI these days. It is getting out of hand. I suspect that there is place for tools like this that help humans to have their understanding in sync with what AI produces. I am looking forward to more new ideas and tools like this. It is upto us to figure this out now!

  • AI-pilling our company: lessons learned

    Good takeaways. This is how most software teams will look like — they will face all the points mentioned in this post and have some version of the agent powering the team.

  • The Bottlenecks for AI-Driven System Design: why principal engineers are not (yet) obsolete

    What is a hill-climbing exercise? I notice this term being used when discussing about performance.

Books

  • Essentialism

    (read 203 pages)

    Finished this book. It gave me a sense of calm and the courage to ask “what is essential here?” whenever I like to.

  • Zen Pencils

    (read 9 pages)

    Make gifts for people - John Green

    Advice for Beginners - Ira Glass

  • Make it Stick

    (read 5 pages)

  • Fahrenheit 451

    (read 32 pages)

    This is going to be the first fiction for me this year. I want to get more into fictional works and enjoy them as much as I enjoy non-fictions. Planning to alternate fiction and non-fiction - let us see how it goes!
